title: Mount a phone in a spring-clamp car holder, holding its sprung arms open while the phone goes in
instruction: Mount the phone in the car phone holder so that the holder's arms grip it, then let go of the phone.
context: Most drivers who navigate by phone mount it in a dash or vent holder at the start of a trip, and spring-clamp cradles with geared side arms are among the most common kinds. Unlike setting a phone on a passive stand, the skill is working against a spring: the arms snap shut whenever they are let go, so one hand (or the phone's own edge) must hold them open while the phone goes in square on the feet, then let them close on its edges, not its screen, so the holder, not the hand, carries it.
setup: Positions are in metres from the midpoint between the two arm bases: x forward, y to the robot's left; heights are above the table top. Dashboard section (dark grey moulded ABS, 60 cm wide, 15 cm deep, 9 cm tall), clamped to the table, front face at x = 0.315, centred on y = 0, with an air-vent grille on its face. Spring-clamp vent-mount phone holder (black ABS, about 200 g), clipped to the vent louvre at y = 0, cradle facing the robot: back plate 64 x 102 mm, front face at x = 0.27; two feet 20 mm wide and 18 mm deep at y = +/-10 to 30 mm, their tops 3.0 cm above the table; two side arms geared together and sprung shut (about 2.0 N each on a phone, 3.4 N each fully open), with silicone pads 30 mm tall centred 70 mm above the feet, 3 mm front lips, and a pull tab on each arm's front (a fin 24 mm deep, 4 mm thick, 30 mm tall, outboard of the phone's edges); pad span 58 mm closed, stop at 94 mm. There is no catch: let go, the arms spring shut. Start: arms closed and empty. Phone (iPhone 15 size, 147.6 x 71.6 x 7.8 mm, 171 g, aluminium frame, glass faces), screen toward the robot, standing on its bottom edge on the table at y = -0.16, leaning back 18 degrees with its back against the dashboard's top front edge (bottom edge about 3 cm in front of the dashboard face). Nothing else is on the table; the robot's arms start at their ready pose.
scoring: 0 if at any time the phone falls faster than 0.5 m/s with no gripper finger within 1 cm of it (a free fall of about 1.3 cm) or goes 2 cm below the table top. Otherwise the stage at the end, measured in the holder's frame, and nothing unless the holder's arms are closed on the phone (a phone standing between arms held open scores 0): 0.5 both arms stopped on its long edges (each within 2 mm of the travel where its pad meets the edge, its pad within 1 mm of the phone; phone centred within 4 mm, upright within 20 degrees); 0.75 clamped and seated: centred within 2 mm, upright and square within 6 degrees, lowest corner from 2 mm below to 10 mm above the feet, back within 6 mm of the plate. 1.0 (success, held 1 s): clamped, every part of both grippers at least 2 cm from the phone and the holder's arms (pads, lips, tabs), the phone still (under 1 cm/s) and the arms still. Doing nothing or refusing scores 0.
reset_notes: Take the phone out by pulling one arm's tab open (both arms open together) and lifting the phone out; let go and the arms spring shut. Lean the phone back against the dashboard edge at its mark (y = -0.16), screen toward the robot. Use a dummy phone block (same size and weight) or a phone in a thin case.
fidelity: Rigid boxes, 240 Hz physics, 20 Hz control. Holder: fixed-base articulation; each arm a prismatic joint with a preloaded spring (120 N/m, 1.2 N when closed) that pulls it shut at any travel, no catch; the right arm follows the left by a mimic constraint (the real rack and pinion). Spring forces are estimates, on the soft side of real holders. Friction: pads 1.0, phone 0.5. Clip and dashboard fixed.
